acceptance: An overlay rule with a tiers selector of deep matches a dispatch whose tier token is opus, claude-opus-*, or deep, and a rule with fast matches haiku (red first)
Rule matching and Policy.OverlayProjection read the dispatch's tier through one canonicalization (TierRank to modelcatalog.CanonicalTiers), with no second copy
The overlay-projections preflight check, or a sibling, warns on a rule tier selector that names no canonical tier
fix: Canonicalize the dispatch tier once where OverlayDispatch is built (or inside matchDim for the Tiers dimension) using the same TierRank/CanonicalTiers path OverlayProjection uses, and extend the preflight check to rule tier selectors.
source: console, 2026-09-30, architecture review of the ADR-0109 fixes (finding 2)
summary: One overlays block reads a dispatch's tier two ways: rule selectors compare the tier string exactly (matchDim(r.Tiers, d.Tier) in go/internal/policy/overlays.go), while overlays.projections maps it through TierRank to a canonical tier name. A rule selecting tiers [deep] therefore misses a dispatch under the concrete token opus. That is the class behind cycle 1779's missing overlay; ADR-0109 fixed it for fable only by removing fable's selector, so any operator rule with a tier selector can still fail silently.
title: Overlay rule tier selectors match the canonical tier, the way projections already do
